newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Mobil head says Argentina key in LatAm strategy.
newsitem.headline: Mobil head says Argentina key in LatAm strategy.

text.p: Lucio Noto, chairman and chief executive of Mobil Corp, said Wednesday Argentina will play a key part in the U.S. oil firm's Latin American strategy.

"I view Argentina as a key element in a regional (natural) gas strategy based on production in Argentina and sales to Chile" and elsewhere, Noto told reporters after a meeting with Argentine President Carlos Menem.

By the end of this year Mobil will have invested some $500 million in Argentina in recent years and Noto said "we will do our best to increase our presence here in coming years." The U.S. company opened its Buenos Aires office in 1987.
Specifically, Mobil hopes to increase its downstream facilities and continue to develop its relationship with Argentine oil company YPF in the years ahead, the chief executive said.

Last September Mobil bought a 28 percent stake in the Sierra Chata gas field and Chihuidos block in the Neuquen basin. The natural gas from the field will be sold to Chile. Separately it has interests in the Noroeste basin.
Noto added, "I am here to acknowledge the (Argentine) government's efforts in conforming to an economic model that makes Argentina attractive for foreign investment."
He said Latin America represents one of the most promising markets for Mobil in the years ahead which is why it is stepping up its presence.

"Energy growth in Latin America has been outpacing most of the world, and we are moving aggressively to capitalize on those opportunities. That is why we have already undertaken a number of different projects."
